output.title: Use the Product Rule Independently
output.rationale: This four-session sequence treats the goal as conceptual learning followed by problem solving. It begins with the meaning and structure of the product rule, then moves through guided differentiation, independent use, and mixed practice. Each session fits a 15-minute window and keeps one main action prominent.

sessions.title: Understand the Product Rule
sessions.objective: Build a clear model of why differentiating a product requires two terms.
sessions.amountLabel: One product-rule model and one complete example
contentTargets: How each term differentiates one factor while preserving the other
completionEvidence: Explain what changes and what stays unchanged in each term
Apply the formula to one example with guidance

sessions.title: Differentiate a Product Step by Step
sessions.objective: Use the product rule procedure on a similar expression with fading guidance.
contentTargets: Substituting power-rule derivatives into the product rule
completionEvidence: Construct the two product-rule terms for a new expression
Solve one polynomial product derivative with minimal prompting

sessions.title: Use the Rule Independently
sessions.objective: Retrieve and apply the product rule without a displayed procedure.
contentTargets: Independent recall of the product rule
completionEvidence: Recall the product rule without assistance
Solve two product derivatives and check both terms

sessions.title: Choose and Apply the Right Rule
sessions.objective: Distinguish product-rule problems from single power-rule problems and repair errors.
sessions.amountLabel: Three mixed classifications and two derivative attempts
contentTargets: Recognizing when the product rule is required
Finding and correcting omitted-factor or omitted-term errors
completionEvidence: Classify three expressions by whether they require the product rule
Solve two mixed problems and correct any product-rule errors

activities.label: Product rule model
activities.title: Why products need two terms
activities.body: Read the model and note the main rule. Then pause before the question.

essentialIdeas: Differentiate a product by taking the derivative of each factor one at a time and adding the two results.

activities.label: Explain the rule
activities.title: Explain the rule in words
activities.body: Say the rule in your own words. Keep it brief.
activities.correctAnswer: Differentiate each factor one at a time and add the two results.
activities.feedback: A complete answer names both terms and the one-at-a-time idea. If needed, repair the missing add-the-two-results part.

activities.label: Repair the gap
activities.title: Fix the missing part
activities.body: Correct the earlier explanation if anything was left out. Write one improved version.
activities.misconceptionSummary: Thinking the derivative of a product comes from changing only one factor instead of adding two one-at-a-time derivatives.
activities.correctAnswer: Differentiate the first factor and keep the second, then differentiate the second factor and keep the first, and add them.
activities.feedback: This should include both one-at-a-time parts and the addition. If one factor was omitted, repair that directly.

activities.label: Explain again
activities.title: State the rule again
activities.body: Give the rule again in plain language. Do not copy the model.
activities.correctAnswer: The derivative of a product is the derivative of the first factor times the second, plus the first factor times the derivative of the second.
activities.feedback: Good if both terms are present and the product structure is clear. If not, add the missing term and try again.

activities.label: Choose the rule
activities.title: Which rule fits here?
activities.body: Pick the rule that matches the expression.
activities.feedback: A product of two changing factors uses the product rule, not the power, constant, or quotient rule.
